doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

chapter: Young Tuxedo and Chris Kelly years
title: Lee Collins and a killing at a dance hall
summary: Bailey recalls a fatal dance-hall incident, first thinking it was Lee Collins, then correcting to Walter Donaldson.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Lee Collins used to play with you? Sure. We used to play with my brother at the offensive band. Oh yeah. Sure. I said Lee Collins was getting killed down Lee County Hall. I'm sure of that. The Jewmaker was all killing by the ladies' friends. That sounds like the truth. I'm telling the truth. Look. You know what's happened? Another folks played at this place, you know? And he went down there and got to dancing with the Jewmaker. The ladies' friends. The Jewmaker's giving her a dance. That's a wild lady. Got to dance with her. And she got sweet on Lee Collins. Lee went to talk with her. She said, take care of man. That's my woman. Don't you put that woman in there. I'll keep care of your man. I said, come on. I said, come on upstairs. I can't leave by the head. I brought them upstairs. Remember that? The man was a killing. Were you playing upstairs in those days? Yeah. They called them. Yeah. The Hall of the New York State was upstairs. And they called them in the cooperators too. And New Hall, that was down on the third and the street. New Hall, played that.
I used to be up on Camp Street. Yeah. I went out and I got in my face. I said, come on. I said, come on up there.
You see that in the head, Lord? I said, I'm getting killed. No, it wasn't Lee Collins. I'll tell you that it was Walter Donaldson.
